prompt_text: Who is the best orthodontist in Columbus Ohio for braces or Invisalign?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single universally “best” orthodontist for everyone — the best choice depends on your needs (age, complexity, preference for clear aligners vs braces), budget, location, and how you weigh experience vs convenience. I can help you find the right provider in Columbus, but here are practical steps and things to look for so you can choose with confidence.

How to find top orthodontists in Columbus
- Use these tools:
  - American Association of Orthodontists (AAO) “Find an Orthodontist”
  - Invisalign provider locator (shows provider experience level)
  - Google Maps / Yelp / Healthgrades for patient reviews and photos
  - Ask your general dentist for a trusted referral
- Prioritize board certification (American Board of Orthodontics) — it indicates extra testing and standards.
- For Invisalign, check the provider’s Invisalign status (Preferred/Platinum/Diamond) — higher tiers treat many cases and have more experience.

Key criteria to compare
- Clinical credentials: orthodontic specialist (not a general dentist doing braces) and ABO board certification
- Experience with cases like yours (complex bite problems vs simple crowding)
- Invisalign experience and provider level (if you want aligners)
- Before & after photos of actual patients
- Patient reviews, especially about results and office experience
- Technology offered: digital impressions (iTero), 3D imaging, CBCT (if needed)
- Cost, payment plans, and insurance handling
- Convenience: office location, hours, emergency policy

Questions to ask at a consultation
- Are you a board-certified orthodontist? How long in practice?
- How many Invisalign/clear aligner cases have you treated (or what is your Invisalign tier)?
- What are my treatment options, estimated treatment time, and total cost?
- Do you use digital scans? Who performs regular adjustments — the doctor or assistants?
- Can I see before/after photos of similar cases?
- What are payment and financing options? What happens if I break a bracket or lose an aligner?

Typical tradeoffs: Braces can handle more complex tooth/bite moves and don’t rely on patient compliance. Invisalign is very popular for adults/teens and works great for mild-to-moderate issues; complexity and provider experience matter for outcomes.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and shortlist well-rated, board-certified orthodontists in Columbus (I’ll need your ZIP or neighborhood), or
- Draft a short message/email you can send to offices to request a consultation and pricing.

Which would you prefer?
